p01.why: A string literal with a suffix calls the operator with a pointer and the length 4.

p02.why: The class converts to a scoped enumeration, and no built-in + takes a scoped enumeration, so no candidate is viable.

p03.why: The class declares only prefix ++, so c++ has no operator.

p04.why: Binary - stays left associative, so (10-3)-2 is 5.

p05.why: s+1 picks the exact member and s+1.0 picks the exact non-member.

p06.why: Only operator() and operator[] can have default arguments.

p07.why: operator() overloads resolve by argument type.

p08.why: Adjacent string literals have two different suffixes.

p09.why: Overloaded = evaluates the right operand before the left, as the built-in does, so trace is 12.

p13.why: Unary & calls the member operator&, which returns 42.

p14.why: The member and the non-member operator+ match equally well, so a+b is ambiguous.

p15.why: A floating literal needs a long double or const char* literal operator, and only unsigned long long exists.

p17.why: A member binary operator with two parameters has three operands.

p18.why: The raw form gets the characters 1.25, four of them.

p19.why: The left operand of a member operator is not converted, and S has no built-in path, so 1 + S(2) has no viable candidate.

p20.why: 12_km calls the unsigned long long form.

p21.why: The block-scope declaration hides the global operator+ and turns off argument-dependent lookup, and (Value, int) is not viable for two Values.

p22.why: Built-in < has no candidate for member pointers, only == and != do.

p23.why: Postfix returns the old value 0, and c ends at 2.

p24.why: No operator function can be variadic.

p26.why: A literal operator cannot be declared at block scope.

p27.why: A non-member postfix -- with an int parameter works and returns the old value.

p28.why: Built-in ++ has no candidate for bool.

p29.why: A literal operator must be a non-member.

p30.why: c++ passes 0 and the explicit call passes 7, so seen ends at 7.

p31.why: Friend literal operators are allowed, and the namespace declaration makes _mi findable; 5*16/10 is 8.

p34.why: a += b uses only operator+=, which V lacks.

p37.why: operator-> returns int, so the chain does not end in a pointer.

p39.why: An operator function can be a template, and there is no main.

p40.why: A non-member operator| for a scoped enumeration gives 3.

p41.why: An unscoped enumeration converts to int for built-in +.

p42.why: Overloaded [] evaluates the left operand first, so trace is 12.

p43.why: -> chains from Outer to Inner to a Target pointer.

p44.why: The raw form gets five digit characters.

p45.why: Both operands convert to int for built-in *, giving 4.

p47.why: With no class operand, operator+(Wrap, Wrap) is not a candidate, and built-in + does not take a scoped enumeration.

p48.why: A literal operator must have C++ linkage.

p52.why: Overloaded >> evaluates the left operand first.

p55.why: Overloaded comma evaluates the left operand first.

p56.why: A static operator() works through an object and by qualified name.

p57.why: A non-member operator needs a class or enumeration parameter.

p58.why: Operator functions can be called by name.

p59.why: The parameter list is not one of the allowed forms.

p60.why: Taking the address of an incomplete class that later overloads & is unspecified, and compilers accept it; there is no main.

p63.why: Overloaded ->* evaluates the left operand first and returns 3.

p64.why: Built-in % takes only promoted integer types, and the class converts only to double.

p65.why: operator[] with no parameters can be called as s[].

p66.why: The long double form gets 3.0 and returns 1.5.

p67.why: operator-> returns A& again, so the chain never reaches a pointer.

p69.why: Overloaded && evaluates both operands, so calls is 2.

p73.why: The specification does not settle this; my guess is that the reference parameters keep the built-in (Color, Color) candidate, and the two tie.

p74.why: A suffix without _ draws a warning, and -Werror turns it into an error.

p75.why: GCC accepts the default argument; Clang and EDG reject it (Q-0060).

p76.why: A non-member converts 1 to S, giving 3.

p77.why: A constexpr literal operator works in static_assert; no main.

p78.why: Pointers to a class do not count as class parameters.

p79.why: operator[] returns a reference that is assigned.

p80.why: Chained << evaluates left to right, so trace is 123.

p81.why: Overloaded += evaluates the right operand first.

p82.why: Overloaded && and || evaluate both operands left first.

p83.why: operator-> may be declared with any return type; it is never used.

p84.why: The numeric forms win over the raw forms.

p85.why: - and * can be unary or binary.

p86.why: Adjacent strings with one or the same suffix join before the call.

p87.why: Only operator() and operator[] can be static.

p88.why: A character literal calls the char form.

p89.why: A plain non-member operator== declaration; no main.

p91.why: Only operator() and operator[] can be static.

p92.why: inner::operator+ hides the global one, argument-dependent lookup searches only m, and (Value, int) is not viable.

p93.why: a[x, y, z] evaluates a then the arguments left to right, also in constant evaluation.

p94.why: operator() can have a default argument.

p95.why: int is not an allowed parameter for a literal operator.

p97.why: The postfix parameter must be int.

p98.why: operator[] can have a default argument and be called with none.
